connections.classification: Provisional newly connected 95e conditional source contract; original 059 q1177 and Segovb L12 391 already identified signed-step-to-speed failure as an open policy. Not a new historical discovery or automatic global unique count; central must reconcile.
connections.first_failed_contract: Every accepted configured step/frequency relationship used to prepare the global IK foot-target speeds should yield a finite nonnegative speed, or be rejected at the owning configuration boundary before publication.

trace.claim: Four step fields are SignedLength; validated IK block checks frequency and other invariants but contains no checks for those four fields or their products.
SignedLength construction/deserialization admits finite negative or positive metres.
All four configured steps are multiplied by frequency and admitted as NonnegativeSpeed before the bundle returns.
Speed admission rejects negative and nonfinite results but accepts zero.
A failure in configured target speeds logs and returns from the system before the owner/rig loop.
Runtime snapshot installation validates and dedicated accessor projects inverse-kinematics config.

connections.conditions_and_limits: An otherwise valid candidate with a finite negative nonzero step and a suitable positive frequency can reach a negative product; sufficiently large finite positive step/frequency can overflow. The shipped values are positive and continuity frequency is 64 Hz (support/08 YAML 275–296). No extreme configuration was parsed, installed or run, no player or visual failure observed, and supported negative/extreme tuning policy remains unresolved. The error rejects the whole IK system before any rig is iterated, rather than corrupting an already-published target. Product execution, native renderer, actual feature scheduling and other configuration ingress paths were not assessed.
connections.future_repair_direction: If such inputs are unsupported, validate the semantic step sign and representable step×frequency relationship at the existing configuration owner; otherwise define an intentional bounded/rejection policy. Preserve valid zero, shipped positive settings, and actual authored behavior. Central owns canonical alias, ledger and implementation.
connections.historical_relationship: 059 q1177 and original Segovb L12 391 already recorded negative-step possibility and left actual allowed tuning/current follower scope open; Adler L11 194 recorded checked conversion. New work connects those original observations to 95e admission and global caller, without transferring earlier authorship.

connections.classification: Current behavioral comparison and unresolved lifecycle/policy question, not an asserted defect.

trace.claim: 95e excludes PoseCulled rigs; P16 query has no such exclusion.
Cull marker is inserted/removed as rig visibility freezes/resumes.
Pose update returns for culled rig and pose-buffer apply skips frozen visibility.
Separately scheduled propagated observation query is not filtered by PoseCulled and can update endpoint/owner-frame memory when terrain, owner, state, rig and finite observations are available.
Source declares chained update and later post-update IK/propagation observer ordering; engine deferred-command timing is not independently verified.

connections.conditions_and_limits: No blanket claim that all IK state or owner_frame freezes during culling: the independent observer can update it. Its early exits and finite/availability guards, the uninspected coordinator remainder, current scheduling, visibility transitions, last-visible contact policy, and actual user-visible consequences remain open. No culling, reentry or animation was executed.
connections.history: Prior ASSESSMENT-L01-HISTORICAL-1370-1374 recorded the query change and explicitly left lifecycle open; baseline q804/q807 preserve culling as a supported mode. ASSESSMENT-POSE-LEG-BOUNDS-95E is a separate previously recorded conditional zero-leg solver case, not this lifecycle question.

nonfindings: The current dedicated IK accessor reads the same animation.inverse_kinematics field from the shared runtime config and maintains its own version-keyed cache (support/06 11–20,24–80). This source comparison does not prove concurrent hot-reload behavior, feature selection or full runtime equivalence.

Terrain blend retains UnitInterval, applies a configured nonnegative ResponseRate and elapsed budget, then readmits the result; a zero rate is permitted by its owner and may intentionally hold state. No defect inferred merely from zero, booleanized desired blend, or native warning text.
Repeated fixed tick gate skips IK when the registered evaluation clock reports no new sample; different clock/source lifecycle and scheduler integration require separate evidence.

The propagated observation owner can update frame and endpoints for an offscreen rig if its prerequisites hold; do not assert no observation or automatically promote its endpoints to evidence of rendered visual quality.

Earlier conditional zero-length leg solve and missing yaw observation records concern distinct owners/first failures; this packet does not establish either and does not transfer prior reviewer credit.

Does the fixed-clock repeat/owner-motion guard preserve intended plant and settle continuity after long offscreen intervals?
What do all unread coordinator ranges, native solver, child modules, rigs and renderer guarantee?
Can the original complete P16 patch be recovered and verified? This packet preserves only the registry assertion and exact role object.

lenses.name: producer-propagation
lenses.assessment: Typed configuration → step/frequency → speed bundle → pre-rig error; pose visibility → IK exclusion and independent observer traced in registered windows. Full renderer and other owners open.

lenses.name: existing-type-owners
lenses.assessment: SignedLength legitimately admits negative offsets; NonnegativeSpeed and AnimationFrequency represent different units/constraints, and their composition needs its own owner contract.

lenses.name: admission-contracts
lenses.assessment: Config validation accepts fields under their type contracts but does not explicitly verify the four step/frequency output relationships. Candidate remains conditional on otherwise valid config and supported policy.

lenses.name: invariant-operations
lenses.assessment: Negative or overflowed step×frequency can fail speed admission before all-rig work. Blend update readmits UnitInterval; no unsupported behavior inferred.

lenses.name: aggregate-states
lenses.assessment: Four independent step/frequency fields are assembled eagerly into one speed bundle. Retained frame/observation and cull modes depend on visibility and separate observer guards.

lenses.name: type-ownership
lenses.assessment: IK authored configuration and checked native target-speed projection own the relationship; unrelated signed geometry owners need not be globally narrowed.

lenses.name: redundant-authority
lenses.assessment: Dedicated IK cache and animation config cache use shared versioned source; separate names alone do not prove conflicting authority. Concurrent publication behavior remains open.

lenses.name: behavior-preservation
lenses.assessment: Exact source diff changes query filter and configuration accessor only. Historical dirty P16 and current 95e are distinct, and no full lifecycle or visual equivalence is asserted.

lenses.name: enum-shapes
lenses.assessment: Enabled, optional terrain, fixed-tick repeat, posture, locomotion ownership and cull are distinct source modes; zero blend response is not automatically invalid.

lenses.name: derivability
lenses.assessment: No safe manual trait/serialization substitution established in actual windows; native modules and unread coordinator remain outside scope.

lenses.name: type-granularity
lenses.assessment: Step length, frequency, derived speed, render sample time, source tick, foot support, local/world frames and configuration state are separate quantities; their relationships matter beyond finite scalar admission.

lenses.name: magic-strings
lenses.assessment: Diagnostic warn/error and instrumentation labels are final text boundaries, not established string-dispatch business state.

lenses.name: magic-numbers
lenses.assessment: The typed rate/time and step×frequency have explicit units. Shipped constants are authored YAML and do not by themselves prove invalid range or require arbitrary clamping.
